A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PredNext research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. The original settings appendix moves from E to H; its retained content can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original action-recognition and retrieval experiments, temporal-consistency analyses, ablations, and appendix KNN training curves.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds loss-weight experiments, backbone-size evaluations, ANN comparisons, and computational measurements in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: The Step Prediction and Clip Prediction components, cross-view objectives, and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged. The added stop-gradient sentence documents target handling without establishing a procedural revision. Deeper backbones extend evaluation of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use UCF101, HMDB51, and MiniKinetics for the same recognition and retrieval tasks, with ImageNet initialization in selected comparisons. The revised MiniKinetics description and additional citations do not establish changed dataset membership or new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 9 substantially broadens the UCF101 comparison to supervised ANN ResNets, ANN SimSiam, ReSpike, SVFormer-st, LSM+STDP, and STS ResNet. These have reported comparison entries, while the original Table 3 comparator set, including rhoSimSiam and CVRL, remains.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce intermediate alpha settings, SEW-ResNet34/50 evaluations, basic versus stronger ANN augmentation, and computational-resource metrics. The established benchmark splits, clip sampling, fine-tuning schedules, and recognition/retrieval metrics remain unchanged. The default alpha value is newly disclosed, not established as changed.

E4.justification: v2 adds complementary analyses of loss balance in Table 8, backbone scaling and pretraining dependence in Table 9, and computational overhead in Appendix E/Table 10. These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond the retained component, prediction-horizon, cross-view, head-size, sampling, and consistency analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 3–7 retain their numerical results, but Tables 8–10 add substantial results on loss weights, comparators, model sizes, and resource costs. For example, Table 9 newly reports 74.1% and 74.2% top-1 accuracy for ImageNet-initialized PredNext-SimSiam with SEW-ResNet34 and SEW-ResNet50. These are additional configurations, not improvements to the earlier ResNet18 results.

T1.justification: New Appendix G introduces semantic/noise variables, different exponential temporal-correlation assumptions, approximate independence, and a mutual-information argument for prediction-based noise suppression. v1 has no corresponding mathematical analysis. The claimed equivalence between the prediction loss and mutual-information maximization is asserted without a derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: plug-and-play cross-view temporal prediction, SNN self-supervised benchmarks, improved representations, and enhanced temporal consistency. Additional experiments do not materially redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for weaker SimSiam/MoCo performance, loss-weight sensitivity, and dependence on backbone size and pretrained-weight quality. It replaces the longer-horizon optimization-difficulty explanation with reduced interaction between nearby timesteps. Appendices F–G further develop spatial-bias and semantic/noise mechanisms, substantially expanding the interpretive account.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states target stop-gradient handling and default alpha=0.5, and Table 10 supplies resource measurements, four-GPU usage, and 16 data workers. Most settings remain unchanged after Appendix E moves to H. The reproducibility statement removes the assertion that supplementary code was submitted, while retaining the prospective public-release promise.

R1.justification: The related-work appendix remains essentially unchanged, but new references support comparisons with additional SNN video methods, spatial-bias discussion, slow-feature reasoning, and MiniKinetics attribution. These broaden research context without substantially revising the original novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. Local edits clarify the LIF description and notation, add explanatory paragraphs and acknowledgments, and update the publication header. New appendices precede the relocated settings appendix, without a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–10 and makes localized presentation refinements: Figures 1–2 receive clearer schematic details, pathway colors, and explanatory captions; caption emphasis and table formatting are revised. Existing empirical plots and retrieval visualizations are retained, with modest resizing and repositioning.

improvement.justification: The alpha sweep, broader comparisons, and measured overhead provide useful evidence for tuning and practical assessment that v1 lacked. Explicit implementation details and clearer diagrams also help readers. These gains are limited by the heterogeneous settings in Table 9 and the unsupported loss–mutual-information equivalence introduced in Appendix G; the revision supports a modest overall improvement.
